notes: Built by scripts/build_identifier_shape_fixture.py to close the parity-corpus gap identified on 2026-08-09: the existing 52 fixture candidates contained ZERO 9-digit CIN shapes, ZERO 10+ digit LONG_ID shapes and ZERO 5+ token phrases, so every parity suite passed against deviations #4/#5 because it could not fail. Expected output is the ORACLE's, including its defects; verify/identifier-shape-parity.ts asserts agreement everywhere except the deviations recorded above, asserts the intended divergence at them, and FAILS on any undeclared difference in either direction.

deviations.reason: CIN_RE/LONG_ID_RE guard against neighbouring DIGITS only, so a digit run inside a longer alphanumeric token matches. Redacting it corrupts the document (proven: https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup/781237504d3f8a9b -> .../[REDACTED]d3f8a9b). DocScrub widens both guards to exclude letters as well. Genuine identifiers delimited by whitespace/punctuation are unaffected.

LONG_ID_RE's (?:\d[\s-]?){10,18} lets the final repetition consume a trailing space, so 'Meeting ID: 826 0122 9711 Passcode' matched INCLUDING the space and redaction yielded '[REDACTED]Passcode'. Restructured to \d(?:[\s-]?\d){9,18}, same 10..19 digit span, cannot end on a separator.

PHONE_RE carried the identical digit-only guard. FOUND BY THIS FIXTURE on its first run, after #4a/#4b had landed and a prior suite had explicitly asserted PHONE_RE was not implicated. An 11-digit run inside a hex blob matched as a phone and redaction corrupted the text. Same guards applied.

FALLBACK_PERSON_RE's {1,3} caps a match at four tokens; a longer capitalized phrase is CUT and the remainder emitted as a second candidate, producing two review units and two replacement spans for one phrase. Raised to {1,5} (six tokens), chosen by measurement against the live document. The ceiling still exists at seven-plus tokens.
